summary_paragraph: The patient with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and known marginal ulcer history was admitted for 5 days of epigastric/right and left upper quadrant abdominal pain with nausea, diarrhea, and dark guaiac-positive stools. She received IV fluids and symptom control, and Gastroenterology performed EGD showing gastritis, a new small ulcer at the gastrojejunal anastomosis, improvement of a larger known anastomotic ulcer, and resolution of a previously seen smaller ulcer; pantoprazole was increased to 40 mg twice daily and sucralfate was continued. Stool testing was negative for H. pylori antigen and two C. difficile toxin tests were negative. CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast showed no bowel obstruction and noted a small left renal hypoattenuation focus without supportive urinalysis findings. Hematocrit was monitored for possible GI bleeding and stabilized/normalized prior to discharge; pain control was transitioned from IV morphine to oral hydromorphone with good effect. She was discharged home tolerating a regular diet, ambulating independently, with plans for repeat EGD in 6 weeks and surgical follow-up within 2 weeks, and return precautions for bleeding or worsening symptoms.
problems: Gastrojejunal ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
